# Vendored third-party code

Everything under `vendor/` is copied verbatim into `dist/chrome/vendor/` by `build/build.mjs` and is used
only by the Chrome host's local image-text detection (OCR). Nothing here is loaded from a network.
`build/validate.mjs` pins the SHA-256 of every vendored script (see `VENDOR_SCRIPT_PINS`), so a changed file
fails the release check until the pin is updated on purpose.

## Tesseract.js (OCR engine, JavaScript side)

| File | Source |
|---|---|
| `tesseract/tesseract.min.js` | `tesseract.js@7.0.0` `dist/tesseract.min.js` (UMD, exposes `Tesseract`) |
| `tesseract/worker.min.js` | `tesseract.js@7.0.0` `dist/worker.min.js` (Web Worker entry) |
| `tesseract/LICENSE-tesseract-js.txt` | `tesseract.js@7.0.0` `LICENSE.md` (Apache-2.0) |
| `tesseract/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` | the `*.LICENSE.txt` notices that ship with those two bundles (buffer, ieee754, regenerator-runtime, zlib.js: MIT / BSD-3-Clause) |

Only change made to the upstream files: the trailing `//# sourceMappingURL=...` comment was removed (the maps are
not shipped, and the store validator rejects source-map references).

## Tesseract.js core (OCR engine, WebAssembly side)

| File | Source |
|---|---|
| `tesseract/core/tesseract-core-relaxedsimd-lstm.wasm.js` | `tesseract.js-core@7.0.0` (Apache-2.0), LSTM-only build, WASM inlined, relaxed SIMD |
| `tesseract/core/tesseract-core-simd-lstm.wasm.js` | same, plain SIMD |
| `tesseract/LICENSE-tesseract-js-core.txt` | `tesseract.js-core@7.0.0` `LICENSE` (Apache-2.0) |

The non-SIMD builds are not shipped: the extension requires Chrome 120, and every Chrome from 91 on has WebAssembly
SIMD (relaxed SIMD from 114). `offscreen.js` picks the relaxed-SIMD file when the browser validates it and the plain
SIMD file otherwise.

## Language data

`tesseract/lang/<lang>.traineddata.gz` are the `4.0.0_best_int` models from the `@tesseract.js-data/<lang>` packages
(version 1.0.0, MIT packaging of the Tesseract `tessdata_best` models, Apache-2.0): int8-quantised "best" models, about a
quarter of the size of the float `best` models with near-identical accuracy. Languages: `eng`, `spa`, `fra`, `deu`,
`por`, `ita`, `rus`. Tesseract.js reads gzip directly (`gzip: true` is its default).

## Sizes (bytes)

| Part | Bytes |
|---|---:|
| `tesseract.min.js` + `worker.min.js` | 174,189 |
| two core builds | 7,805,239 |
| seven language models | 12,826,406 |
| licences and notices | 23,331 |
| **Total** | **20,829,165** |

## Why the code scan allows two idioms in these files

`build/validate.mjs` forbids `eval`, `new Function`, `Function("...")`, remote imports and network APIs in the
extension's own code. The vendored bundles contain these idioms, all in dead code paths of well-known libraries:

* `worker.min.js`: webpack's global-object probe (`this || new Function("return this")()`, only reached when
  `globalThis` is not an object) and regenerator-runtime's `Function("r", "regeneratorRuntime = r")(r)` fallback (only
  reached when `globalThis` is not an object).
* `tesseract.min.js`: the same regenerator-runtime fallback.
* The core builds contain Emscripten's browser/node loader branches (`XMLHttpRequest`, `fetch`); the WASM is inlined,
  so no request is made.

None of this is remote code: every script that can run is packaged, and the extension-page CSP
(`script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`) does not include `unsafe-eval`, so the `Function` fallbacks would throw
rather than run even if reached. The validator therefore allows these idioms only in the pinned files below; any
other file under `vendor/` is held to the same rules as our own code, and `eval(...)` is never allowed.

The default `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/...` strings in the bundles are the library's fallbacks for when `corePath` /
`langPath` are not given. `offscreen.js` always passes local `chrome.runtime.getURL(...)` paths, and the test in
`test/chrome/ocr-extension.mjs` fails if the offscreen document makes any request to a non-extension URL other than
the image being scanned.

## Updating

1. `npm pack` / install the new `tesseract.js` and `tesseract.js-core` (and `@tesseract.js-data/*`) in a scratch
   directory (never inside this repository).
2. Copy the same files listed above, strip the `sourceMappingURL` comment, update this file and the pins in
   `build/validate.mjs`.
3. `npm run package`, then `node test/chrome/ocr-extension.mjs`.

## @noble/ed25519 (term-update signature check)

| File | Source |
|---|---|
| `noble-ed25519/noble-ed25519.js` | `@noble/ed25519@3.2.0` `index.js` (MIT), classic-script wrapper generated by `feed/tools/vendor-noble.mjs`; exposes `self.nobleEd25519` |
| `noble-ed25519/LICENSE-noble-ed25519.txt` | the package's `LICENSE` (MIT) |

Used only by the service worker (`importScripts`) to verify the Ed25519 signature on the downloaded spoiler term list
(`hosts/chrome/feed.js`). Why vendored rather than WebCrypto: `crypto.subtle` Ed25519 only exists from Chrome 137, and
raising `minimum_chrome_version` from 120 would drop installs for no gain; the library is ~900 lines, dependency-free,
and its only hash (SHA-512) comes from `crypto.subtle.digest`. The upstream `index.js` (SHA-256
`a4f631d1876b5d9e43a86cd71194ca27b5e1451edf4ba4db9a418f40a475569a`, tarball integrity
`sha512-criDgRlnUA09hchYrTy/JUWPIEap5rZxQe6wDWzRx51oWWpDRcUpuNzlgPxDJaOK6AsW9c0wKcj3rKRv6t+bPQ==`) is checked by the
generator; only the ES-module `export` line, an enclosing function and `\uXXXX` escapes for non-ASCII characters in
comments differ. The generated file is SHA-256 pinned in `build/validate.mjs`.
